title: I’ve been building a 3D sports autobattler with ChatGPT, but I could really use some advice on the battle screen
author: No-Engineering-1387
selftext:
I’ve been working on a game called Battle Ball, which is basically my attempt at creating a new kind of fantasy sport built around autobattler mechanics.  
You build a team, choose your formation, and your athletes play the match on their own. They’ll pass, tackle, shoot, and use different abilities while trying to score against the other team’s Reactor.  
I’ve been using ChatGPT to help with the code, gameplay systems, and debugging, and Meshy for the 3D character models.  
I’m happy with the direction the gameplay is heading, but there’s something about the battle screen that I feel could be better.  
I want the arena to look more interesting without making it harder to actually see what’s happening on the field.  
I’ve been considering adding more detail to the background, maybe some kind of futuristic stadium, spectator stands, or a more industrial arena setting.  
But I’m also worried about adding too much visual clutter or hurting performance, especially on mobile.  
Here’s some actual gameplay footage.  
What would you change about the battle screen? Does the arena need more detail, better lighting, a different camera angle, or something else entirely?  
And if you’ve worked on something similar, how did you make the environment feel alive without distracting from the gameplay?  
I’d appreciate any feedback, even if it’s critical.
